newsitem.title: USA: VLSI noted Q4 growth in consumer segment.
newsitem.headline: VLSI noted Q4 growth in consumer segment.

text.p: VLSI Technology Inc said it experienced "substantial growth" in the consumer digital entertainment and communications segments in its fourth qaurter but that the growth was offset by expected downsides in its personal compute-related businesses. As a result, revenues were about flat with year-ago levels.
Still the company was able to resposition itself toward the growth markets while sustaining revenues, Alfred Stein, chairman and chief executive officer said in a statement.
Stein added that VLSI "resolved key manufacturing issues" by deciding to end production in its San Jose chip plant.
It also brought its newer facility in San Antonio, Texas, up to world-class performance levels, he said.

Earlier, VLSI reported a fourth quarter net loss of $63.6 million, or $1.38 per share, which includes a pre-tax charge against earnings of $115.6 million associated with ending production at its San Jose chip semiconductor wafer fabrication plant.
Without the charge, the company would have earned a profit of $8.1 million, or $0.17 per share, still down from net income of $18.3 million or $0.38 per share a year ago.

VLSI said it experienced year-over-year revenue growth in both the networking and wireless businesses of approximately 40 percent. It said it continues to benefit from the rapid adoption of digital wireless technology worldwide.
